conclusion: Two copies of the APOE rs429358 C allele. In the 2026 cross-trait analysis of the largest longevity GWAS meta-analysis this variant is the shared causal signal at the TOMM40/APOE/APOC1 cluster, and the ApoE e4 allele it defines is associated with a lower likelihood of surviving past the 90th survival percentile; a 2026 case-control study of disease-free Super Seniors found reduced odds of healthy aging in e4 carriers. Which APOE isoform you actually carry depends on rs7412 as well as this site, so read the two rows together. A population-level association, not a prediction about one person, and not medical advice.

One copy of the APOE rs429358 C allele. The reported association with lower odds of longevity and of disease-free survival past 85 is intermediate between the two homozygous genotypes. Isoform assignment also depends on rs7412.

No copy of the APOE rs429358 C allele, so no ApoE e4 allele from this site. This is the more common genotype in most populations and carries no e4 longevity signal. It says nothing about the e2 allele, which is read at rs7412.

Two copies of the APOE rs7412 T allele, the ApoE e2-determining allele. A 2026 cross-trait genetic analysis reports this variant as acting opposite to e4 on longevity, and a 2025 analysis identified the alternative C allele as the most prominent variant limiting extreme human longevity. An association at population scale, not a forecast for one person.
negatives: ApoE e2 homozygosity is the usual genetic background of familial type III hyperlipoproteinaemia, a lipid disorder that needs a second trigger to become manifest; ClinVar carries rs7412 under that condition with an expert-panel review status. A longevity-favourable allele here is not favourable for every outcome.

Two copies of the FOXO3 rs2802292 G allele. FOXO3 is one of the few longevity loci confirmed at genome-wide significance across independent GWAS meta-analyses; a 2026 GWAS of disease-free Super Seniors found this variant among FOXO3 variants nominally associated with increased odds of healthy aging, mainly in women, and a 2025 Southern Italian cohort study reported a protective effect of the G allele. The effect on one person's lifespan is small and heavily modified by everything that is not genetic.

Reported in a December 2025 bioRxiv preprint that ran affected sib-pair linkage analysis in 212 sibships enriched for ancestral longevity and prioritised 12 rare protein-altering variants in seven genes inside the linked regions.
